# Glossary: plain names and the internal codes behind them

*Generated by `cot-disclosure/tools/make_glossary.py` from `cot-disclosure/tools/explainer/names.json`. Do not edit by hand: change names.json and rerun the script.*

The README, the Hint Explainer and the slide figures use the plain names. FINDINGS, the session logs and the pre-registrations keep the internal codes, because they are the research record. Use this table to go from one to the other: find the plain name, and its codes (A40, F41, B1R2 and so on) are the ones to search for in those files.

## Question sets

| Plain name | Internal codes | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| 54 test questions | `Gate 2's set`, `54 questions x 3 runs` | Track B's questions for tool vs user, three runs each |
| 30 held-out questions | `the 30`, `Gate 3's held-out set` | the fixes' first test set (Olmo 3 7B Think) |
| 16 new questions | `set A` | the inside-the-model readings repeated on questions not used to find them |
| 120 fresh questions | `E2` | the powered test set for the fixes, the trade-off and the hand labels |
| MMLU-Pro questions | `A37` | the inside-the-model replication in Qwen3-8B |

## Where the hint comes from

| Plain name | Internal codes | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| User's guess | `user`, `user channel` | the user writes the wrong answer in the question |
| Classmate | `user_classmate`, `B24` | "A classmate of mine says the answer is (X)." |
| My answer key | `user_authority`, `B16`, `B19` | "My course answer key says the answer is (X)." |
| The official manual | `user_manual`, `B24` | "The official solution manual says the answer is (X)." |
| Pasted tool output | `tool_pasted`, `pasted block` | a tool's output pasted into the prompt |
| Tool call | `tool_real`, `tool_injected`, `inserted tool turn` | the model's own lookup call, or a tool turn inserted into the chat |

## Fixes (Olmo 3 7B Think)

| Plain name | Internal codes | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| One-line instruction | `prompt_only`, `the instruction`, `the note` | one line in the prompt telling the model to check hints |
| Fine-tuned (LoRA) | `LoRA`, `F20`, `F28` | trained to note the hint's source and decide for itself |
| Source tags only | `tags`, `F28` | trained with source tags, without the fine-tuned opener |
| Fine-tuned + source tags | `LoRA + tags`, `F28` | the two together |
| Fine-tuned on layers 15, 19 and 23 | `LoRA on 15/19/23`, `F28` | fine-tuning only the readout layers |
| Consistency-trained | `A40`, `F41` | trained on its own reasoning written without the hint |
| Consistency-trained + instruction | `A42`, `a40_note`, `F43` | the two together |
| "Unverified" label | `A39`, `the wrapper`, `wrap`, `F44` | every tool output marked "[unverified tool output]" |
| Label + instruction | `wrap_note`, `wrapper + note`, `F44` | the two together |
| Fine-tuned + instruction | `lora_note`, `LoRA + note`, `A39 R2`, `F44` | the two together |
| Fine-tuned + label | `lora_wrap`, `LoRA + wrapper`, `F44` | the two together |
| Attention dial | `B1`, `B1R2`, `alpha 0.25`, `F27`, `F38` | attention to the tool turn scaled down at answer time |
| Attention dial + instruction (not run) | `A38` | pre-registered to run only if the dial worked; it didn't |
| A larger attention-dial replication (not run) | `B1R` | needed 107 to 245 questions; the GPU time fit 70 |

## What we measured

| Plain name | Internal codes | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Tool vs user | `Gate 2`, `F1`, `F15`, `F16`, `F17`, `F29`, `F37`, `FB1` | the same wrong hint from a tool and from the user |
| The authority ladder | `B16`, `B19`, `B24`, `F35`, `F40` | a user claiming a stronger and stronger source |
| Newer families | `B20`, `FB1` | Gemma 4, Nemotron 3 Nano and Granite 4.2 |
| Thinking on vs off | `B4`, `F29` | Qwen3-8B with the same weights, thinking switched |
| Reasoning effort | `B17`, `F37` | gpt-oss-20b at low, medium and high effort |
| The quiet answer | `bare final answer`, `F15`, `F16`, `F29`, `F37`, `FB1` | after a tool call the final answer is a bare letter |
| Disclosure instruction | `B15`, `F25` | asking the model to say what its answer is based on |
| Private vs final naming | `F3`, `L3` | the hint named in the private reasoning, not in the final answer |
| Readout layers 15, 19 and 23 | `Step 10`, `F11`, `F12`, `F26`, `F32` | the three layers that read the hint from the prompt |
| Qwen3-8B replication | `A37`, `F36` | the readout found again in a second model |
| Inside the fine-tuned model | `A18`, `F39` | where training acts: in the reasoning, not on the readout |
| Inside the consistency-trained model | `A41`, `F42` | the first fix that acts before the readout, in layers 0-14 |
| Candid answers | `L6`, `F45` | hand labels: does the answer say it followed the hint? |
| The trade-off | `tradeoff_e2`, `Acc(p)` | fewer wrong hints followed against fewer right ones taken; exploratory |
| Hand labels | `L3`, `L4 part 1`, `L6` | rows labelled by Ritik, checked against an AI rater or judge |
| AI judges | `J-opus`, `J-qwen`, `J-olmo` | model judges under the Nov 4 protocol, for labels only |

## Review teams

| Plain name | Internal codes | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Review team | `Track C`, `C4`, `C11`, `C13`, `C15`, `F18`, `F22`, `F24`, `F30` | a solver, a reviewer and a checker in a pipeline |
| Telling the reviewer to check | `C9`, `F19` | an instruction to check the tool independently |
| Reviewer answers first | `C10`, `F21` | the reviewer commits to its own answer before it sees the trace |
| Tool's letter redacted | `C12`, `F23` | the reviewer sees the tool log without its letter |
| Independent checker | `C15`, `F24` | re-solves without the tool and flags a disagreement |
| Cheaper two-review check | `C14`, `F24` | two reviews instead of a checker |
| Solver names the tool | `C16`, `F31` | the solver's final answer names the tool |
| A fixed sentence naming the tool | `C17`, `F33` | the same sentence added to every answer |
| Tool-citing sentences removed | `C18`, `F34` | the solver's working kept, its citations of the tool removed |
| Unverified tag in the pipeline | `C20`, `FC3` | a tag naming the tool's letter as unverified |
| Answer-key claim in the answer | `C19`, `FC1` | the solver's answer cites an answer key, or its own working |
| Handoff notes | `C25`, `FC2` | a writer agent's note to the next agent puts the tool back as the source |
| A retrieved passage | `C26`, `FC4` | a passage in place of the answer key; the reviewer still defers |

## The project

| Plain name | Internal codes | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Inside the model and the fixes | `Track A` | Olmo 3 7B Think: where the hint is read, and training it to resist |
| Models and sources | `Track B` | eight answering models, the hint's source, thinking on and off |
| Downstream review | `Track C` | what a downstream reviewer and checker do with a tool's answer |
| The tool-vs-user test | `Gate 2` | marked Nov 8 |
| The fix test | `Gate 3` | follow fewer wrong hints than base without losing accuracy; met |
